obligation: Internal report of a suspected incident (all staff and subcontractors)
trigger: Any workforce member or subcontractor suspects an incident
deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: SOC (24x7 line) or the on-call incident commander
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CJIS Security Addendum in 24 contracts; POL-03 applies the same rule to all incidents

obligation: Company notice to each affected criminal justice agency (24 agencies on ACMC or legacy hosting)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6b; Security Addendum; agency contracts; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Suspected incident that may involve CJI or CHRI
deadline: IR-6b sets no separate deadline. Contracts and POL-03 4.4: within 1 hour of discovery, without waiting for the investigation; written fact sheet within 4 hours
notify: Each agency's local agency security officer, who routes to the CJIS Systems Officer (CSO), SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official, and FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Agency report of a contractor security violation to the CSO and the FBI (agency duty)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 Appendix H, Security Addendum sec. 4.01-4.03
trigger: Security violation involving a contractor with CJI access
deadline: Addendum sets no deadline; follows the state CSA's procedure
notify: The agency reports to the CSO and the Director, FBI; the FBI may suspend access and require CHRI to be returned or deleted
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; the company supplies its actions and evidence on request

obligation: Company notice to each affected revenue agency (6 agencies) of a possible FTI disclosure
citation: N92-R01: Pub. 1075 Exhibit 7 I(3), I(13) (contracts); Pub. 1075 sec. 1.8.2; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, including an incident in an FTI tenant, its backups, or its file transfers
deadline: Immediately. Company target: within 1 hour of discovery, so each agency has most of its 24-hour window
notify: Each agency's disclosure officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: TIGTA and IRS Office of Safeguards report of an FTI incident or data breach
trigger: Discovery of a possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI; do not wait for an internal investigation
deadline: Immediately, and no later than 24 hours after discovery
notify: TIGTA (for network intrusions, the TIGTA office the publication names) and the IRS Office of Safeguards (data incident report with no FTI in it)
applies_at_this_tier: Agency files. Sec. 1.8.2 also places the duty on any person who discovers a possible improper disclosure, so the company confirms with each agency within the 24 hours and reports directly if it cannot confirm

obligation: Media release involving FTI (agency duty)
trigger: A media release about an incident involving FTI
deadline: Before distribution
notify: IRS Office of Safeguards receives the draft from the agency
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; company statements about FTI tenants go through the agencies

obligation: Business associate notice to AG-04 (security incident and breach of unsecured PHI)
citation: N92-R03: 45 CFR 164.314(a)(2)(i)(C); 164.410; AG-04 business associate agreement
trigger: Security incident affecting AG-04 ePHI; breach of unsecured PHI
deadline: Security incident: per the BAA (5 business days; company target 1 hour). Breach: without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (164.410(b)), with the identity of each individual and the information AG-04 needs for 164.404(c) notices
notify: AG-04 privacy and security officers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - AG-04 environment only
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee or agent other than the person committing the breach (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: AG-04 notices to individuals, HHS, and media (covered entity duty)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI of AG-04 enrollees
deadline: Individuals and media: without unreasonable delay, no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; HHS: at the same time if 500 or more, otherwise within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: Affected individuals; HHS; prominent media if more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: AG-04 duty; the company may send notices on AG-04's behalf if the BAA or AG-04 asks

obligation: Notice to the IES human services agencies (SNAP, TANF, Medicaid applicant data)
trigger: Unauthorized access to IES applicant or household data
deadline: The cited rules limit use and disclosure but set no contractor notice deadline. Contracts and POL-03 4.4: within 1 hour of discovery for a suspected incident; written fact sheet within 4 hours
notify: Each agency's information security officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - through the 4 IES contracts

obligation: Notice to AG-05 (motor vehicle records)
trigger: Unauthorized access to DPPA personal information
deadline: The DPPA has no breach notice provision. AG-05 contract: within 24 hours (company target 1 hour); driver license numbers also trigger state breach laws
notify: AG-05 records officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract; DPPA liability (18 U.S.C. 2724) shapes the response

obligation: Florida state agency ransomware report (AG-01, AG-03)
trigger: Ransomware incident at a state agency, including one in a contractor-hosted system the agency uses
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center and the Cybercrime Office of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company notifies the agency within 1 hour and supplies the required content: summary of facts, date of the most recent backup and its location, whether it was affected and whether it is cloud-based, types of data, estimated fiscal impact, and ransom demand details
clock_starts: Agency discovery (in practice, the company's call)

obligation: Florida county and municipality ransomware report (Florida local government customers)
trigger: Ransomware incident affecting a county or municipality
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, the FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff with jurisdiction over the local government
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for about 37 Florida counties and cities. AG-02 (a sheriff's office) decides with its county whether 282.3185 reaches it, and gets the company's notice within 1 hour either way

obligation: Florida local government after-action report
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident at a county or municipality
deadline: Within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; the company provides the incident summary, resolution, and lessons learned in time

obligation: Prohibition on ransom payment by Florida agencies
trigger: Ransom demand to a state agency, county, or municipality
deadline: Applies at all times
notify: Not a notice. Shapes the ransom decision (POL-03 4.7)
applies_at_this_tier: Binds Florida customers; the company will not pay over any agency's objection

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to each affected Florida agency
trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information) in a system the company maintains for an agency
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida agency (the covered entity), with all information it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies directly to the company as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h))
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Agency notice to Florida individuals
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; law enforcement may request a delay in writing
notify: Each affected Florida resident
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty. The company may send notices on an agency's behalf if asked (501.171(6)(b))

obligation: Agency notice to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; the company supplies counts of Florida residents per agency

obligation: Agency notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty if more than 1,000 are notified

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Affected individuals who live in the other 15 customer states or anywhere else
deadline: Varies by state; vendor-to-data-owner notice duties also vary
notify: Each affected agency (vendor notice); residents and regulators under each state's law (agency duty in most cases)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - outside counsel's state matrix; the company supplies residence data

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Any cybersecurity incident that may be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
notify: Disclosure committee records the determination, its date and time, and its reasoning
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (EDGAR), through the filing agent
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company

obligation: SEC Form 8-K amendment
trigger: Required information was not determined or unavailable at the time of filing
deadline: Within 4 business days after the information is determined or becomes available
notify: SEC (EDGAR)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Attorney General delay of the Item 1.05 disclosure
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay of up to 30 days, extendable as the item allows
notify: Request through outside counsel to the Department of Justice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, only with a written Attorney General determination

obligation: Annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report (10-K)
deadline: With the 10-K
notify: Investors (10-K Item 1C)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the incident and lessons learned are considered for the next disclosure

obligation: DoD cyber incident report (if the CUI enclave is affected)
trigger: Cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it
deadline: Rapidly report: within 72 hours of discovery, through the DIBNet portal, with a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate
notify: DoD (DIBNet)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the DoD subcontract; the enclave is isolated from ACMC, so this applies only if the review under (c)(1)(i) finds the enclave affected

obligation: Malicious software submission and media preservation (DoD)
trigger: A reported cyber incident under 7012(c)
deadline: Submit isolated malware to the DoD Cyber Crime Center; preserve images and relevant packet capture for at least 90 days from the report
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3); DoD on request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, with the 7012(c) report

obligation: Incident report number to the prime contractor
trigger: The company reports a cyber incident to DoD as a subcontractor
deadline: As soon as practicable
notify: The prime contractor
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, with the 7012(c) report

obligation: Covered telecommunications report
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification, then a further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (or as the clause directs)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - federal contracts; unlikely in a ransomware response but checked during forensics

obligation: Kaspersky covered article report
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: A covered article (Kaspersky Lab products or services) identified during contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification, then a further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - federal contracts; checked during forensics

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability

obligation: Law enforcement and CISA report (voluntary)
citation: OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) mitigating factor; company practice
trigger: Ransomware or data theft confirmed
deadline: Company target: within 24 hours of declaration
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary; coordinated with the agencies, which may have their own law enforcement reporting duties

obligation: Supply chain incident coordination
citation: SP 800-53 IR-6(3) (Moderate baseline); CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6(3)
trigger: Incident involving a cloud provider, SaaS vendor, or subcontractor in the attack path
deadline: As soon as practicable
notify: Cloud provider security channels; affected vendors and subcontractors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract (SP 800-53 Moderate)
clock_starts: Discovery of the supply chain link

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring any response vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: CIRCIA covered incident and ransom payment reports
citation: N92-R07: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: no final rule in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. Recheck when a final rule is published

obligation: Notice to other agency customers (local governments and others)
trigger: Incident affecting a customer's tenant or data
deadline: Per contract (most require 24 to 72 hours); company target: within 1 hour for any affected tenant
notify: Each customer's named security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contract
